summary: Added Textarea, the multi-line field, from the approved 'Component --- Text Area' sheet. It is a separate component rather than a prop on Input because the two differ on the keyboard (Enter submits an Input and inserts a newline here) and on how height is expressed (rows, not a size step) -- one component would have to branch on both. What it DOES share is the control surface: rounded-md, border-[1.5px] border-edge-subtle, bg-field, the inset and type of the matching size, the focus-within border+ring with its forced-colors outline fallback, and the derived hover/invalid/disabled states, all identical to Input. That claim is asserted as a RELATIONSHIP in the browser test -- it mounts a real Input at the SAME SIZE beside the Textarea and compares computed radius, border width, border colour, fill, inset and type size -- rather than as numbers, which would pass while the two drifted apart. Sizes lg/md/sm are DERIVED from Input's table rather than drawn: inset and type step exactly as Input's do (px-md py-sm / p-sm / px-sm py-xs, 14/12/12px), while the height cannot carry over, because Input's is a constant and this one is `rows` line boxes -- the same rows gives 127.125 / 111.5625 / 103.5625px, measured. The three are asserted to differ from each other and to be monotonic, which is the assertion Badge lacked when its two sizes shipped pixel-identical. Leading is leading-snug at every size: the sheet stored a raw 18px on 14px type, a ratio of 1.286 off the --ui-leading-* scale entirely, and snug is the nearest role at 0.2px per line -- it also lands the 6-row lg box on the sheet's own 128px. One deliberate divergence from Input, documented in the doc's forwarding block: the inset padding sits on the <textarea> rather than on the control wrapper. The native resize grip is painted at the textarea's own corner and the drag sets an inline height on it, so padding on the wrapper would float the grip 12px inside the box and clip the drag instead of growing with it; the inset a user sees is identical, and clicking it now lands on the field rather than on dead wrapper padding. `cols` is OMITTED from the props type rather than forwarded: the control is w-full, so a character count never reaches layout -- measured, cols={5} rendered at the same 412px as no cols at all -- and a prop that is accepted, set as an attribute and inert reads as supported. isResizable (default true) is vertical-only, since a field draggable wider breaks the layout containing it, and is withdrawn along with the field when isDisabled. Label, helperText, errorText, isRequired, isInvalid and the aria-invalid/aria-describedby wiring are Input's contract unchanged, error announced before helper.

migration.manual: Nothing to migrate -- this is a new item. A multi-line field previously had to be hand-rolled or an Input stretched with className, both of which lost the label/error wiring; replace those with <Textarea label="..." rows={n} />. `size` matches Input's, so a form already using size="md" fields gets a matching textarea. `cols` is a TYPE ERROR rather than a no-op: size the field with className on the outermost node.
